chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-Harith ibn Muhammad, from Bureyd Al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had relations with his wife on a day he was making up from the month of Ramadan, he (peace be upon him) said: If he had relations with her before the decline of the sun, there is nothing upon him except one day in place of one day; and if he had relations with her after the decline of the sun, then upon him is that he gives charity to ten poor people; if he is not able, he should fast one day in place of one day, and fast three days as an expiation for what he has done.

key_terms.يَوْمٌ مَكَانَ يَوْمٍ: One day in place of one day

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man who has intercourse with his wife while making up a missed Ramadan fast?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific expiation (kaffarah) for breaking a make-up fast (qada) through sexual intercourse, distinguishing between pre- and post-solar noon (zawal) incidents. It establishes a graded penalty where post-noon intercourse requires both the makeup day and a dual expiation of feeding ten poor or fasting three days, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the severity of breaking qada compared to Ramadan fasts. This ruling highlights the importance of intention and timing in Shia fiqh, linking physical acts to spiritual accountability.
